question: The average of the first five prime numbers greater than 20 is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**32.2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first five prime numbers greater than 20 are 23, 29, 31, 37, and 41.
 
• To find the average, add these prime numbers: 23 + 29 + 31 + 37 + 41 = 161.
 
• Divide the sum by the number of prime numbers: 161 / 5 = 32.2.
 
• Therefore, the average of the first five prime numbers greater than 20 is 32.2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Numbers**

 
 
• Prime numbers are natural numbers greater than 1 that have no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.
 
• The first ten prime numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, and 29.
 
• 2 is the only even prime number; all other prime numbers are odd.
 
 
 
• **Average Calculation**
 
 
• The average (or mean) of a set of numbers is calculated by dividing the sum of the numbers by the count of the numbers.
 
• Formula: Average = (Sum of all elements) / (Number of elements).
 
 
 
• **Properties of Prime Numbers**
 
 
• Prime numbers have exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and the number itself.
 
• They are used in various fields, including cryptography and number theory.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Prime Numbers**
 
 
• Prime numbers are fundamental in the study of number theory.
 
• They play a crucial role in modern computer encryption algorithms.
